etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: From Old French ars bouterez (noun, literally “supporting arcs”), from bouterez (adjective), oblique plural of bouteret (rare in the singular), from Frankish *bôtan, from Proto-Germanic *bautaną (“to push”). Ultimately cognate with beat.
senses: (architecture) A brick, concrete or stone structure built against another structure to support it.
(by extension) Anything that serves to support something; a prop.
To support something physically with, or as if with, a prop or buttress.
(figurative, by extension) To support something or someone by supplying evidence.
